title: Soap bar volume
observableEvidence: Computes the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by multiplying length, width and height, and labels the result in cubic units.
prompt: A bar of soap is shaped like a rectangular prism 7 1/2 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 2 1/2 centimeters thick. What is the volume of the soap bar? Include the unit in your answer.
solutionMethod: Multiply the three edge lengths (writing mixed numbers as fractions), simplify, and label the result in cubic centimeters.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Whole-answer match after case, spacing and trailing-punctuation normalization; no substring parts. The cubic-centimeter unit is required: a bare number, or the number with a linear or square unit, is not accepted.

hintSteps.prompt: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height, even when some edges are fractions.
hintSteps.question: Which three lengths will you multiply?

hintSteps.prompt: Multiplying the whole number first can make the fractions easier to handle.
hintSteps.question: What is 7 1/2 times 4?

hintSteps.prompt: A different bar is 5 1/2 cm by 2 cm by 1 1/2 cm: 11/2 × 2 × 3/2 = 11 × 3/2 = 16 1/2 cubic centimeters.
hintSteps.question: Using the same steps, what is the volume of this soap bar, and what unit does it have?

accessibilityNotes: Text-only item: every length needed is in the prompt, so no figure or color is needed. The answer is typed in one box and must include its unit.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A bar of soap is a rectangular prism seven and one-half centimeters long, four centimeters wide, and two and one-half centimeters thick. Find its volume and write the unit.
